evidence_labels.HIST: historical archive, market data and model scores collected before the freeze

question: Does the Lopez-Lira & Tang post-news trading design, with headlines scored by the chronologically consistent ChronoGPT-Instruct 1.55B classifier using its authors' FAVORABLE/UNFAVORABLE/UNCLEAR prompt, earn a positive same-session return after realistic costs in US equities 2016-2026, among firms present in the 2026-09-21 asset master?
why_this_study: Earlier price-based early-entry studies failed after costs (mover v1 0/768 rule-exits, v2 0/244; a broad price/volume scan found volatility, not direction). A primary-source review ranked LLM headline direction first and rated it plausible: it is the only candidate effect shown to hold outside its model's training window, but it decays and breaks even near 20 bps per round trip. This study removes look-ahead by scoring every headline with a model whose training cutoff precedes it.

source_paper.citation: Lopez-Lira, A. and Tang, Y., Can ChatGPT Forecast Stock Price Movements? Return Predictability and Large Language Models, arXiv 2304.07619v6 (30 Oct 2025); SSRN 4412788

facts_confirmed_from_pdf_text.data_p13_14: CRSP common stocks (share codes 10/11) with news matched to RavenPack, relevance score 100, 'event similarity days' > 90, stock-gain/stock-loss headlines excluded, same-day near duplicates (Optimal String Alignment similarity > 0.6) removed; Oct 2021-May 2024; 159,137 firm-headline-date observations, 4,123 firms; 82% overnight.
facts_confirmed_from_pdf_text.model_p16: gpt-4-0314 (training data to Sep 2021), temperature 0; YES -> 1, UNKNOWN -> 0, NO -> -1.
facts_confirmed_from_pdf_text.timing_p19: News before 9 a.m. on a trading day: enter at that day's open, exit at that day's close. News after the close: enter at the next open, exit at the next close. Daily rebalanced, equal weight. Footnote 20: at least two firms per leg, otherwise only the other leg is entered.
facts_confirmed_from_pdf_text.table1_p51: Overnight drift, gross: long-short mean 0.34%/day, Sharpe 2.97, hit rate 58.06%; long 0.08%/day; short-only portfolio mean -0.26%/day (Table 5: N+ 69, N- 20). Intraday drift in Table 1 is measured close-to-next-close (0.50%/day, Sharpe 2.63).
facts_confirmed_from_pdf_text.costs_p20_fig4_p46: Cumulative return above 300% at 5 bps round trip, above 100% at 10 bps, unprofitable at 20 bps; costs modelled as fixed round-trip bps because trades execute in open/close call auctions.
facts_confirmed_from_pdf_text.decay_p35_fig8_p50: Annualized Sharpe of the overnight strategy: 6.54 (2021Q4), 3.68 (2022), 2.33 (2023), 1.22 (Jan-May 2024).
facts_confirmed_from_pdf_text.intraday_p22_23_table3_p54: Headline-level regressions: score coefficient 0.027 (t=1.32) for 1-15 min after release; 0.189 (t=5.12) from 15 min after release to that day's close; 0.116 (t=2.31) close to next close.
facts_confirmed_from_pdf_text.size_p22_p35: Small-firm interaction 0.404 (t=4.75) for overnight drift; after negative news large caps (top size tercile) show no drift while small caps keep drifting.
facts_confirmed_from_pdf_text.footnote30_p35: The same-day intraday drift strategy is hard to implement because the number of intraday releases per day, hence position size, is unknown in advance.

critiques_considered: Glasserman & Lin, arXiv 2309.17322: part of the effect is a distraction effect from entity names in the prompt.
Sarkar & Vafa (ICML 2025): prompting a model to ignore later knowledge does not remove look-ahead.
Lopez-Lira, Tang & Zhu, arXiv 2504.14765: LLMs memorize financial data, so in-window tests are contaminated.
Chronologically consistent models avoid look-ahead by construction: ChronoGPT (He, Lv, Manela, Wu; arXiv 2502.21206) and DatedGPT (arXiv 2603.11838). This study uses ChronoGPT-Instruct.

models.family: ChronoGPT-Instruct v1 (manelalab/chrono-gpt-instruct-v1-<YYYY>1231), MIT licence, not gated, about 1.55B parameters (52 layers, dim 1536, 12 heads), context 1,792 tokens, GPT-2 BPE via tiktoken 'gpt2'
models.year_mapping: A headline whose created_at falls in New York calendar year Y is scored by the (Y-1)-12-31 checkpoint; Y >= 2025 uses 2024-12-31. Headlines before 2016 are dropped (no checkpoint strictly before them in the pinned set, and their sessions lack 20 prior daily bars anyway). news_signal.checkpoint_year.
models.runtime: ~/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/tools/vllm-0.30.0/bin/python used read-only (torch 2.13.0+cu130, tiktoken 0.14.0); nothing installed. GPU RTX 5090 Laptop; process capped at 12 GiB by torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction; measured peak 10.17 GiB at batch 32 / 3,072 batch tokens with the cached decoder.
models.security: See checkpoints.json load_policy: weights and config.pt only through torch.load(weights_only=True); ChronoGPT_instruct.py imported from the verified local file after its sha256 matches; from_pretrained and remote-code loaders never used; HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and a local TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR in the scoring process; every file's sha256 verified at download and weights re-verified at each load.
models.numerics: float32 weights and float32 activations with TF32 disabled (torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, float32 matmul precision 'highest'). The reviewed forward hard-casts activations to bfloat16 in exactly two methods (ValueEmbedding.forward line 201, ChronoGPT.forward line 232); score.install_fp32_forwards replaces those two methods with line-for-line copies without the casts (plus an optional last_positions gather before the per-position final norm and lm_head). See scoring.numerics_evidence.

scoring.paper_prompt_verbatim:
Forget all your previous instructions. Pretend you are a financial expert. You are a financial expert with stock recommendation experience. Answer “YES” if good news, “NO” if bad news, or “UNKNOWN” if uncertain in the first line. Then elaborate with one short and concise sentence on the next line. Is this headline good or bad for the stock price of company name in the short term?
Headline: headline
scoring.paper_prompt_ascii_template:
Forget all your previous instructions. Pretend you are a financial expert. You are a financial expert with stock recommendation experience. Answer "YES" if good news, "NO" if bad news, or "UNKNOWN" if uncertain in the first line. Then elaborate with one short and concise sentence on the next line. Is this headline good or bad for the stock price of {company} in the short term?
Headline: {headline}
scoring.instruct_wrapper: not used by the operative variant (kept for llt_upstream_wrapper): news_signal.chrono_format, the exact string ChronoGPT_instruct.extract_response() builds
scoring.company: news_signal.clean_company_name(asset-master name): security-type tails such as 'Common Stock', 'Class A Common Stock', '(The)' removed
scoring.headline: news_signal.clean_headline: HTML entities decoded, whitespace collapsed
scoring.decoding: greedy (argmax); at most 16 new tokens; stop at EOS (50256) or once news_signal.label_decided (the first word of the first non-empty line is followed by a non-letter, or that line has ended)
scoring.parse: Stored label (unchanged): news_signal.parse_label, the model authors' strict rule - the first word of the first non-empty line (quotes, markdown and an 'Answer:'/'Response:' prefix removed) must equal FAVORABLE, UNFAVORABLE or UNCLEAR; anything else is stored as PARSE_FAIL (0). evaluate.check_scores validates every stored label against its raw output. Position (operative, D22): news_signal.operative_score on the same first word - prefix UNF -> -1, FAV -> +1, UNC -> 0, anything else PARSE_FAIL (0); context overflows are PARSE_FAIL.
scoring.context_overflow: prompt tokens + 16 > 1,792: not generated, stored as PARSE_FAIL with stop 'context_overflow'
scoring.no_rescoring_rule: After the freeze no event is rescored, and no alternative prompt, model, parse rule or decoding setting is evaluated against outcomes of this dataset.
scoring.operative_prompt:
Below is an instruction that describes a task. Write a response that appropriately completes the request.

### Instruction:
Classify this news headline as either FAVORABLE, or UNFAVORABLE, or UNCLEAR for the stock price of {company}.

### Input:
{headline}

### Response:
scoring.operative_prompt_source: He, Lv, Manela & Wu, 'Instruction Tuning Chronologically Consistent Language Models', arXiv 2510.11677: section 3.3 (the prompt the model's authors use for prompt-based trading portfolios on firm news headlines, 'similar to Lopez-Lira and Tang (2023)', classified by the first generated word; ChronoGPT-Instruct-Realtime H-L annualized mean 8.17%, Sharpe 0.95, next-day close-to-close, Jan 2007-Jul 2023) and section 2.2 (their Alpaca-style SFT format with the preamble 'Below is an instruction that describes a task. Write a response that appropriately completes the request.'). {company} is the cleaned firm name; a name already ending in '.' is not given a second period.

labels.other: PARSE_FAIL, scored 0: the authors' rule assigns any first word other than favorable/unfavorable to the unclear portfolio

variants_compared.llt_alpaca: the paper's prompt (ASCII quotes) as the Instruction and the headline as the Input, in the Alpaca format; labels YES/NO/UNKNOWN
variants_compared.hlmw_alpaca: the model authors' classification prompt (operative_prompt); labels FAVORABLE/UNFAVORABLE/UNCLEAR
variants_compared.llt_upstream_wrapper: the paper's prompt inside ChronoGPT_instruct.extract_response()'s wrapper (system prompt, empty Input); labels YES/NO/UNKNOWN

variant_selection.why: A first probe (2026-09-25, 256 events, 2024 checkpoint, bfloat16) of the paper's prompt in the upstream wrapper returned 248 PARSE_FAIL and 8 UNKNOWN: the 1.55B model mostly echoes 'Headline: ...' instead of answering YES/NO. Three variants were then compared on the same label-agnostic sample (50 events per checkpoint, smallest sha256(event_id); 500 events).
variant_selection.rule_v1_superseded: valid-label rate >= 0.90 and each direction >= 5%, first eligible in preference order llt_alpaca, hlmw_alpaca, llt_upstream_wrapper. Probe in bfloat16 (on the events file before guard B was corrected): llt_alpaca 48/500 valid, hlmw_alpaca 483/500 (FAVORABLE 188, UNFAVORABLE 285, UNCLEAR 10), llt_upstream_wrapper 21/500 -> hlmw_alpaca.
variant_selection.rule_v2_operative: news_signal.select_variant: directional labels >= 50% of the probe and each direction >= 5%, same preference order. Amended before any outcome because float32 decoding (adopted for the numerics evidence below) turns some 'UNFAVORABLE' answers into malformed words such as 'UNFLEXIBLE' (62/200 on one 2023 sample), which both rules score 0, so the v1 valid-rate threshold measured decoding noise rather than prompt compliance.

probe_v2_float32.sample: 50 events per checkpoint by smallest sha256(event_id) from events.jsonl.gz sha256 103187845992933dc1716e6bb26aea3332db8caa3939aefef4c77c1dc74bb0cb; identical event set for all three variants

variant_selection.label_agnostic: only label counts were used; no price or return was read

numerics_evidence.bfloat16: same 32 prompts (2023 checkpoint): logits move by up to 0.59 between batch 1 and 32 identical unpadded rows and by up to 0.63 with right padding alone, while top-1/top-2 margins were 0.06-1.23 (many below 0.45); bf16 batch-32 vs batch-1 labels agreed on 160/200 and shifted FAVORABLE from 51 to 29.
numerics_evidence.float32: same prompts: max logit difference 0.0 between batch 1, batch 32 and padded rows; batch-32 vs batch-1 labels 40/40.
numerics_evidence.tf32: tensor-core float32 matmuls agreed with exact float32 on 196/200 labels at about 1.6x the speed; not adopted.

decoder.validation: raw outputs identical to the full-recompute decoder on 400/400 events (2023 checkpoint) and 300/300 (2016 checkpoint); second-step logits differ by at most 8.6e-5; 32.9-35.4 vs 9.7-10.5 events/s
decoder.per_run_check: --check-batch1 16: 16 events per checkpoint are rescored alone and their labels compared

scoring.prior_evidence: The model authors' own test of this prompt (arXiv 2510.11677, Table 4) found an H-L annualized mean of 8.17% (about 3 bps/day gross, next-day close-to-close, Sharpe 0.95). Modelled costs here are about 4-5 bps per position round trip (about 9 bps/day for long-short), so a net pass requires a same-session effect several times larger than that estimate.
scoring.paper_prompt_ascii_template_note: the paper prompt with ASCII quotes and {company}/{headline} placeholders, used by the tested llt_* variants (not operative)
scoring.score_row_checks: evaluate.check_scores: exactly one score row per liquid-lane event (refuse if any is unscored or duplicated); for every used row: checkpoint_year = news_signal.checkpoint_year(created_at), revision, weights and code sha256 = checkpoints.json, variant/template/dtype/matmul/decoder = pinned_settings, prompt_sha256 = the event's own prompt, and label/score reproduce from raw_output. Small-lane events without a row are left out and counted.

operative_rule.sensitivity: the strict rule (stored labels, evaluate.position_side rule 'strict') is evaluated on the same data and reported beside every item as strict_rule_sensitivity; it never opens a gate
operative_rule.chosen_from: output text only, 2026-09-25, before the freeze; no price or return was read

news.archive: ~/.local/state/native-agent-stack/research/data-lake/news/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>.jsonl.gz (Alpaca news API, Benzinga), 2015-01-01..2026-09-23; run-header records 2,213,433 records; 2,217,343 lines read on 2026-09-25 (2 repeated ids dropped)
news.symbols_field: a string holding a list, JSON or Python-literal; parsed with json.loads, else ast.literal_eval (literals only)
filters_in_order: F1 parseable created_at and unique id
F2 symbols parse to a list; exactly one symbol (relevance proxy)
F3 symbol resolves to exactly one asset in the 2026-09-21 asset master (active preferred over inactive)

F4 primary operating company: exchange in NYSE/NASDAQ/AMEX/ARCA/BATS; no .WS/.W/.U/.R/.RT suffix; name does not match the broad-universe fund pattern ETF|ETN|Fund|Trust|Shares|ProShares|Direxion|iShares|SPDR|Index|Portfolio nor the security-type pattern Warrant(s)|Unit(s)|Right(s)|Preferred|Note(s)|Debenture(s)|Depositary|Ordinary Share|Subordinated|Cert.|Certificate(s)|Perpetual
F5 timing window overnight or RTH (see timing), trade session within 2016-01-04..2026-09-18
F6 timestamp guard A: updated_at before the window's decision cutoff (overnight: strictly before 09:00 NY on the session; RTH: at or before release + 15 min)
F8 not a price-movement headline (news_signal.MOVEMENT_PATTERNS; 'sell' removed and 'up'/'down' may not be followed by 'to' after the D5 audit)
F9 novelty: no article mentioning the same symbol (any symbol count) with the same normalized headline in the prior 24 h, articles ordered by (created_at, id)

F11 timestamp guard B: estimated ingestion time = max(created_at, 90th percentile of the created_at of the 100 articles with the next-lower news ids) must be before the window's decision cutoff (overnight: strictly before 09:00 NY; RTH: at or before release + 15 min); news_signal.estimated_ingestion / ingestion_guard
F12 liquidity lane from prior-session daily bars (see universe); RTH additionally requires the liquid lane
F13 first headline per (symbol, session, window) by (created_at, id)

timestamp_measurements_pre_freeze.guard_B_history: v1 (median of 101 centred ids, created > 1 h earlier) and v2 (median of the 5 lower ids) were replaced before any outcome, on review: guard B now compares an estimated ingestion time with the window's own decision cutoff. New counts are in receipts/prepare-summary.json.

d5_audit.method: 200 headlines drawn with random.Random(20260925).sample from the 131,566 single-symbol archive headlines that the narrowed filter drops (sorted by news id); labelled from text only by the builder
false_positives: market-wide move ('Stocks Up ~1.5% Just Ahead Of ... FOMC Minutes')
analyst note quoting a past move (Deutsche Bank on Apple)
d5_audit.narrowing: before the audit, 'sell' (163 single-symbol hits alone in Mar/Jun 2021-2024, mostly 'Offering ... By Selling Stockholders') was removed and 'up'/'down' followed by 'to' ('Up To $8.4M') no longer matches
d5_audit.reading: B headlines carry firm news but state the market's reaction; they are dropped, as the paper drops RavenPack stock-gain/stock-loss items; this removes some news events (limitation L12)

timing.calendar: blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/data/session-calendar.json (XNYS via exchange_calendars 4.13.2, early closes included), sha256 44f0ebf7c82ceee6a1fd2beceeca38c5a1e894c723bbc7c0ac677f452f592b5c
timing.rule: With s the first session whose official close is after the release time t (America/New_York, DST-aware through zoneinfo; weekends, holidays and early closes follow from the calendar): [close(s-1), 09:00 on s) -> overnight, enter at s's official open, exit at s's official close; [09:00, open(s)) -> excluded (paper convention); [open(s), close(s) - 30 min) -> RTH, enter at t + 15 min, exit at s's official close; [close(s) - 30 min, close(s)) -> excluded. Intervals are half-open. news_signal.Calendar.classify.
timing.sub_windows_reported: overnight events are labelled pre_open (released on the session date) or post_close (released earlier); both trade identically

universe.daily_bars: ~/codex-ecosystem/state/broad-market-20260921/dataset/daily.parquet (raw_* columns; 2016-01-04..2026-09-18); only sessions strictly before the trade session are read
universe.lane_rule: news_signal.lane_for on the 20 XNYS sessions before the trade session, all of which must have a bar: liquid if the prior session's raw close >= $5 and the median raw close x raw volume >= $20,000,000; small if raw close >= $1 and median >= $2,000,000 and not liquid; otherwise ineligible
universe.identity: Daily bars, auctions and minute bars are keyed by the ticker current on their collection date (provider default asof); news symbols are the tickers as published. Renamed or reused tickers can join a headline to another issuer (limitation L1).

prices.auctions: GET https://data.alpaca.markets/v2/stocks/auctions (feed sip) for every event symbol-session, collected before the freeze (collect_auctions.py); raw entries stored
prices.auction_selection: news_signal.select_auction_price: (1) auction print (O open / 6 close) at a tape code of the current listing venue (NASDAQ: Q or T; NYSE: N; AMEX: A; ARCA: P; BATS: Z); (2) else the print of the only non-Arca venue with one; (3) else the print of the only venue with one; (4) else the official-price condition (Q open / M close) at the listing venue; else the event is excluded and counted
prices.rth_entry: news_signal.rth_entry_quote / rth_entry_price: the first two-sided, uncrossed SIP quote stamped in [release + 15 min, +60 s] from GET /v2/stocks/quotes collected for every liquid RTH event; longs pay its ask, shorts receive its bid; no quote -> excluded and counted. Minute bars are no longer used (their per-year top-500 membership used same-year volume).
prices.exit: official close of the trade session by the auction selection rule, for both windows
prices.no_adjustment: entry and exit fall in the same session, so raw prices need no corporate-action adjustment

costs.auction_slippage_justification: Market-on-open/close orders fill at the official auction price; a $10,000 order is far below auction size for names with >= $20M median daily dollar volume. 2 bps per side is a stated allowance for fill and impact risk, not a measurement; 10 bps for the descriptive small-cap lane. Break-even costs are reported so any allowance can be compared.

fees.rule: news_signal.sale_fees_usd on the sale leg (long exit, short entry): SEC Section 31 rate on sale notional plus FINRA TAF per share with its per-trade cap (none when the price is below the per-share rate); Alpaca commission 0
fees.date_basis: trade date (the SEC rate's charge date is the settlement date; the difference only matters within two sessions of a rate change)
fees.before_first_row: sessions before 2016-02-16 use the earliest SEC row (21.8 $/M; the in-force FY2015 rate was lower, so this is conservative)

costs.short_leg: no borrow fee (positions open and close in the same session). Shorts flagged under SEC Rule 201 from pre-decision information (short_sale_restriction) are excluded from confirmatory items and reported; locate / easy-to-borrow availability is not modelled (L5)
costs.net_return: news_signal.position_net_return: fills moved adversely by the per-side costs, shares = notional / entry fill, P&L net of fees divided by notional
costs.rth_entry: entry at the quote side (ask for longs, bid for shorts) plus rth_entry_allowance_bps; exit at the official close with the auction allowance

portfolios.rule: news_signal.daily_portfolios per window x lane on positions excluding Rule-201-flagged shorts: score +1 long, -1 short, 0 no position; each leg is the equal-weight mean of its positions and exists only with >= 2 names; the confirmatory long-short = long leg + short leg and exists only on days with both legs. The paper's version (single leg when only one exists, footnote 20) is reported descriptively as long_short_paper with the number of single-leg days.
portfolios.tradable_leg: the long leg is the one a long-only paper account can trade

segments.justification: Every headline is scored by a checkpoint whose training cutoff precedes it, and nothing is fitted on returns, so the whole period is out of sample for the scorer and is used once, confirmatorily. overnight_full and rth_full start at the first session with 20 prior daily bars (RTH entries are now priced from SIP quotes, so the minute-bar range no longer limits them). recent_24m tests the documented decay. paper_window and years are descriptive.

items.hypothesis: mean daily net long-short return > 0 (days with both legs)
mean daily net long-leg return minus the benchmark > 0
mean daily net long-short return > 0 for entries 15 minutes after intraday releases, held to the close
mean daily net long-short return > 0 in the most recent 24 months

items_justification: Break-even >= measured cost equals 'mean net > 0' under a fixed cost model, so it is reported descriptively rather than tested. NEWS-4 tests decay; NEWS-2B tests selection skill for a long-only account; NEWS-2 keeps the absolute long-leg test.

inference.statistic: one-sided t of the mean daily net return with a Newey-West (Bartlett) variance
inference.item_rejected: days >= min_days and rejected in its family (primary fixed sequence, or its secondary Holm member); days < min_days -> insufficient_sample
inference.non_rejection_reading: report the one-sided 95% upper bound (mean + 1.645 x NW se) of the mean net and mean gross daily return, and whether it lies below 3 bps/day (model authors' estimate) and 34 bps/day (the paper)

gates.long_only_paper_candidate: the secondary LONG-ONLY member (NEWS-2B and NEWS-2 jointly) rejected AND the overnight liquid long-leg mean net return in recent_24m > 0 (point estimate)
gates.long_short_candidate: NEWS-1 and NEWS-4 both rejected in the primary fixed sequence
gates.failure_rule: If no gate is met the result is recorded as a failure of this preregistered specification; no post-hoc prompt, model, threshold, lane or window variant is promoted from this dataset.

minimum_detectable_effect.formula: MDE = (z_{1-alpha_item} + z_{0.80}) x sigma / sqrt(N), one-sided, 80% power, Newey-West inflation ignored

expected_days.overnight_full: about 2,600 (2,672 sessions carry liquid overnight events; days with both legs are fewer)
expected_days.rth_full: at most 2,673 sessions carry liquid intraday events

minimum_detectable_effect.error_bound: the two families at 0.05 each bound the chance of any false gate at 0.10
minimum_detectable_effect.reading: The prior for this classifier is about 3 bps/day gross (model authors), far below the full-segment MDE (5-11 bps/day) and below modelled long-short costs (about 9 bps/day): NEWS-1 is expected to fail. Its value is the upper bound and the break-even estimate. An effect of the paper's size (34 bps/day gross) would be detected.

descriptive_only: gross and net long, short and long-short for every window x lane x segment, with Sharpe and daily hit rate
label distribution and parse-failure rate by checkpoint

deviations.what: The study tests the LLT trading design with the ChronoGPT-Instruct 1.55B classifier, not gpt-4-0314
deviations.why: Removes look-ahead by construction; the prior for this classifier is about 3 bps/day (model authors), so this is not a replication of GPT-4's 34 bps/day and a null does not refute the paper.

deviations.what: Alpaca/Benzinga news with a single-symbol tag as the relevance proxy instead of RavenPack relevance 100
deviations.why: No RavenPack licence; a single-symbol tag is the nearest available 'predominantly about one firm' signal.

deviations.what: Operative prompt: the model authors' headline classification prompt (FAVORABLE/UNFAVORABLE/UNCLEAR, Alpaca format), not the Lopez-Lira & Tang prompt
deviations.why: ChronoGPT-Instruct does not answer the paper's prompt in its YES/NO format (56/500 directional in float32; 29/500 in the upstream wrapper); the model's authors published this prompt for the same headline-to-portfolio task. The paper's prompt is kept verbatim and was tested.

deviations.what: Only the first answer word is decoded (greedy, <= 16 tokens)
deviations.why: The label depends only on the first word (the model authors' rule); greedy decoding makes that word identical to the one a longer generation would start with.

deviations.what: Regex exclusion of price-movement headlines instead of RavenPack stock-gain/stock-loss categories
deviations.why: Category not available; patterns listed in news_signal.MOVEMENT_PATTERNS and checked by synthetic tests.

deviations.what: Instrument filter from the current asset master (reused broad-universe fund pattern plus a security-type pattern) instead of CRSP share codes 10/11
deviations.why: No CRSP; the reused pattern keeps the definition consistent with earlier mover studies; the security-type pattern removes warrants, units, rights, preferreds and notes that the fund pattern misses.

deviations.what: First headline per symbol per window instead of aggregating all headlines per firm-day
deviations.why: A deterministic rule that avoids choosing among later, overlapping headlines; the paper's same-day near-duplicate removal is approximated by the 24 h exact-duplicate rule.

deviations.what: Intraday lane enters 15 min after release at the SIP quote (ask/bid) and exits at that day's official close; releases in the last 30 minutes are excluded
deviations.why: Matches the paper's significant intraday window (Table 3, 0.189, t=5.12); quotes replace minute bars because the minute-bar universe used same-year volume (look-ahead) and dropped 93,618 events.

deviations.what: Official SIP auction prints and explicit fees plus allowances instead of CRSP open/close and flat 5/10/20 bps
deviations.why: Measures executable prices and costs for the account that would trade.

deviations.what: Newey-West one-sided tests with Holm over four items
deviations.why: The paper reports Sharpe ratios and cumulative returns without a preregistered multiplicity rule.

deviations.what: 2016-2026 instead of Oct 2021-May 2024
deviations.why: Chronologically consistent checkpoints make every year out of sample; the paper's window is reported descriptively.

deviations.what: Two timestamp guards: updated_at before the decision cutoff, and an ingestion-time estimate from id predecessors before the decision cutoff
deviations.why: Alpaca does not guarantee created_at is the publication time and the archive stores the last version of each article.

deviations.what: Checkpoint by New York headline year; 2025-2026 headlines use the 2024-12-31 checkpoint
deviations.why: Strictly earlier cutoff for every headline; no newer checkpoint is published (gap up to 21 months).

deviations.what: Float32 activations instead of the upstream bfloat16 casts
deviations.why: In bfloat16 the logits move by 0.6-0.9 with batch shape or padding, more than typical label margins, so labels depended on batch composition (160/200 agreement); float32 is batch-invariant (max difference 0.0) and evaluates the stored float32 weights at full precision.

deviations.what: Batched, key/value-cached greedy decoding
deviations.why: Throughput (about 3.4x); outputs identical to full recompute on 700/700 validation events and to batch size 1 in float32; a 16-event batch-1 check runs per checkpoint.

deviations.what: SEC fee applied by trade date; the earliest SEC row before 2016-02-16
deviations.why: Charge-date differences are at most two sessions around a rate change; the earliest row overstates the FY2015 rate (conservative).

deviations.what: Operative prompt selected by outcome-blind label compliance; the selection rule was amended after the probe
deviations.why: v1 (valid-label rate, bfloat16) and v2 (directional share, float32) both select hlmw_alpaca, so the amendment had no effect on the choice; only label counts were read.

deviations.what: Labels FAVORABLE/UNFAVORABLE/UNCLEAR instead of YES/NO/UNKNOWN
deviations.why: They belong to the operative prompt (D3); the mapping to +1/-1/0 is the same.

deviations.what: Confirmatory long-short requires both legs (>= 2 names each)
deviations.why: A single-leg day is a directional bet, not a long-short; the paper's single-leg version is descriptive.

deviations.what: Rule 201 short-sale restriction flags
deviations.why: A restricted short cannot be sold at the bid; flagged shorts are excluded from confirmatory items.

deviations.what: Benchmarked long leg (NEWS-2B) and a fixed-sequence plus Holm multiplicity design
deviations.why: Review fix: a long leg can be positive because news days rise; the benchmark isolates selection.

deviations.what: Operative score by the unique three-letter prefix of the first answer word (UNF -> -1, FAV -> +1, UNC -> 0, anything else PARSE_FAIL 0) instead of the authors' exact-word rule; the exact-word rule is reported beside every item
deviations.why: In float32 greedy decoding the model often starts 'UNF' and continues with another token ('UNFLEXIBLE', 'UNFRIENDLY', 'UNF'): 59,673 of the 59,803 strict parse failures of the current events (99.8%) begin with 'UNF', and they are 31.2% of the 2023 checkpoint's outputs and 26.0% of 2024's, so the exact-word rule would silently drop a quarter to a third of the negative calls in NEWS-4's segment. The three label words have unique three-letter prefixes. Decided before the freeze from output text only; no price or return was read.

limitations: L1 Ticker identity: news symbols are as published while daily bars, auctions and minute bars use collection-date tickers; 948 candidates had no daily bars at all and other renamed or reused tickers can join silently to another issuer.
L2 Company names and exchanges are current (asset master of 2026-09-21), not as of the headline.
L3 (retired) The minute-bar universe is no longer used; RTH entries are priced from SIP quotes.
L4 The ChronoGPT-Instruct model card states its instruction data were filtered to pre-2000 content; pretraining is year-bounded per checkpoint.

L5 Shorts assume the stock is easy to borrow and can be located at the open or 15 minutes after release; Alpaca's easy_to_borrow flag is current, not historical, and is not applied. Rule 201 is handled separately (short_sale_restriction).
L6 The RTH daily equal-weight normalization uses the day's event count (paper footnote 30); per-event dollar P&L is implementable, the daily percentage is not known in advance.
L7 News coverage grows over time (18,585 selected events scored by the 2015 checkpoint vs 104,614 by the 2024 checkpoint), so early years carry fewer names per leg.
L8 Timestamp guards reduce but cannot remove the risk that created_at precedes public availability.

L9 Label mix varies by checkpoint vintage (float32 probe, 50 events each: e.g. the 2022 checkpoint labels most headlines UNFAVORABLE), so leg sizes shift across years; portfolios are formed within a day, where one checkpoint scores all headlines of that calendar year.

L10 Output malformation varies with the checkpoint vintage. Share of current-event outputs that fail the authors' exact-word rule: 2015 0.09%, 2016 1.56%, 2017 0.05%, 2018 0%, 2019 0.19%, 2020 0.01%, 2021 7.42%, 2022 0.03%, 2023 31.17%, 2024 26.04% (the re-check's 31.2/26.0/7.8% counted superseded rows too); 99.8% of them begin with 'UNF'. Under the operative prefix rule (D22) at most 0.12% of any checkpoint's outputs remain PARSE_FAIL. The strict-rule sensitivity shows how much the confirmatory results depend on D22.

L11 Survivorship: single-symbol headlines whose ticker is absent from the 2026-09-21 asset master are dropped (prepare.py F3). The missing share falls from 30.3% of single-symbol headlines in 2016 to 4.2% in 2026 (reviewer's per-year count; the rerun's counts are in receipts/prepare-summary.json diagnostics.survivorship_*). Delisted and renamed firms are therefore under-represented in early years; every verdict is scoped to firms present in the 2026-09-21 asset master (protocol scope).
L12 The movement filter drops headlines that carry firm news together with the stock's reaction (22% of the D5 audit sample).

L13 Guard B (estimated ingestion after the decision cutoff) drops intraday events very unevenly by year: 2016 16.2%, 2017-2020 6.8%-15.5%, 2021 39.4%, 2022 30.1%, 2023 26.4%, 2024 0.3%, 2025-2026 0%; overnight 1.5% overall (at most 7.8%, 2019). The fall to zero from 2024 points to a change in how the feed assigned news ids (for example batch- or back-filled ingestion before 2024) rather than in publication delays; intraday items are the most exposed because their cutoff is only 15 minutes after release. NEWS-3's sample therefore shifts toward 2024-2026 and toward promptly ingested articles; the table is receipts/prepare-summary.json diagnostics.guard_B_drops_by_window_and_session_year and year-by-year intraday results are descriptive.

freeze_procedure: 1 finish scoring every event (receipts/scoring-status.json): every liquid event has exactly one row with the pinned settings; record label distribution, parse failures and batch-1 agreement
2 independent pre-outcome re-check of this protocol and the code; resolve findings
3 run evaluate.py --print-pins and confirm it equals protocol.json#/pins (regenerate if any pinned file changed), then set status frozen_pre_outcome, frozen_before_outcomes true and frozen_at; commit
4 copy receipts/freeze-record.template.json to receipts/freeze-record.json with protocol_sha256 (sha256 of the committed protocol.json) and protocol_commit (that commit); commit
5 run evaluate.py on a clean tree; it refuses any other state
no_outcome_statement: Up to this draft no return, P&L, hit rate or post-decision price change has been computed on real data, and no open was paired with a close; only the computations in pre_freeze_computations were run.
pre_freeze_computations: C1 prepare.py over the news archive: parsing, symbol counts, asset-master membership (and its share by year), timing-window assignment, timestamp guards (updated_at vs cutoff; estimated ingestion from id predecessors vs cutoff), movement-headline and duplicate flags, first-per-window selection; funnel counts and the updated_at - created_at distribution
C2 liquidity lanes and the Rule 201 carry-over flag from daily bars of sessions strictly before each trade session
C3 (retired 2026-09-25) minute-bar file existence; minute bars are no longer used

C4 auction collection and materialization: request/response tallies and counts of symbol-sessions with an official open, close or both, and which selection step supplied them (no open and close were combined)
C5 SIP quote collection at RTH entry times: whether a valid entry quote exists and its half-spread distribution (the entry quote only; no exit price was read with it)
C6 model downloads with sha256 verification; tokenizer file verification

C7 model scores on events (all prompt variants in probes, the operative variant in the full run): raw outputs, labels, label distributions, parse failures, batch-1 agreement, throughput and GPU memory
C8 numerics diagnostics: logit differences between batch shapes, dtypes, TF32 and the cached decoder on real prompts
C9 D5 audit: 200 dropped headlines labelled from text
C10 strict versus operative (D22) label counts of the stored outputs by checkpoint and lane (output text only)
scope: All verdicts apply to firms present in the 2026-09-21 asset master (Alpaca; current names, exchanges and tickers). Firms delisted or renamed before that date are under-represented (limitation L11), so results do not generalize to the full historical cross-section.
expectation_before_freeze: NEWS-1 is expected to fail. The model authors report about 3 bps/day gross for this prompt (next-day close-to-close, 2007-2023), while modelled costs are about 9 bps/day for the long-short. The confirmatory value of NEWS-1 is its one-sided 95% upper bound on the mean net and gross return and the break-even round-trip cost, read against 3 bps/day and 34 bps/day.

short_sale_restriction.rule: news_signal.ssr_flag: overnight - carry-over only: the prior session's split-adjusted low <= 90% of the close of the session before it (both before the trade session); RTH - that carry-over, or the entry quote's bid <= 90% of the prior session's raw close
short_sale_restriction.treatment: flagged shorts are excluded from every confirmatory item; descriptive tables report their count and the long-short including them
short_sale_restriction.limitation: a Rule 201 trigger before the open of the trade session (pre-market) or an intraday trigger followed by recovery before the RTH entry is not detected

benchmark.news_2b: long leg net minus the same-day equal-weight net return of holding every scored liquid overnight event long from the official open to the official close (all labels, same costs)
benchmark.why_not_spy: The benchmark isolates the classifier's selection within the same news-day, same-lane, same-timing, same-cost population, so a positive NEWS-2B cannot come from news days or the market rising; SPY would credit the average news-day return and needs data outside the event set.

primary.reason: the long-short gate needs both; NEWS-4 is tested only if NEWS-1 is rejected

secondary.member_p: the largest p among the member's items (intersection-union test, Berger 1982): the LONG-ONLY member is rejected only if both the benchmarked and the absolute long-leg tests are
secondary.reason: Holm (m=3) over NEWS-1, the benchmarked long leg (jointly with the absolute long leg) and NEWS-3; replaces the earlier gatekeeping step (NEWS-2 at 0.05/3 after NEWS-2B), which could add up to 0.05/3 of false rejections outside the Holm family

multiplicity.error_bound: Each family bounds the probability of any false rejection at 0.05 (fixed sequence and Holm control the familywise error strongly; the intersection-union member is a level-0.05 test of the union null). Every gate opens only on rejections in one family, so the probability that any gate opens falsely is at most 0.05 + 0.05 = 0.10.
